03 · CREW SELF-CHECK

How are you today?

Your report feeds ARES’s observation-selection policy. It stays in this tab session for reload recovery; the separate mission replay retains its fixed synthetic telemetry.

Use the time you actually slept, not time spent in bed. An estimate is acceptable; note uncertainty to the crew.

Choose how you feel now compared with your usual day. This is a self-report, not a mental-health diagnosis.

Report new or worsening symptoms even if the sensor readings look normal.

What do these readings mean?

Sleep and HRV-derived features are compared with Morgan’s own synthetic reference because personal changes may matter more than a generic number. Cabin CO₂ is an environmental clue, not a measure of blood oxygen or proof of a medical cause. Wearable and cabin sensors can fail or drift; confirm unexpected readings and follow the mission protocol. No value here clears someone for duty.

04 · NEXT JUSTIFIED STEP

Measure what helps resolve the uncertainty.

In this demonstration, a three-minute vigilance replay tests whether performance has shifted relative to Morgan’s own baseline. ARES then updates its explanation and checks the action policy.

  1. Review the signals and crew report.
  2. Open the synthetic incident and approve the recommended observation.
  3. Select an observed or counterfactual result to see the decision change.

ARES does not diagnose or prescribe treatment. Severe or rapidly worsening symptoms require the mission’s emergency protocol and a qualified crew medical authority. Operational actions in this prototype are simulated.

3-minute vigilance check

This is a synthetic replay of a short attention test, not a live test. In an operational protocol, the crew would follow an approved procedure, respond to prompts for three minutes, and compare response latency with the same person’s prior baseline.

Why this check? It may show whether performance changed before a demanding task. A slower response does not diagnose sleep loss or establish fitness for duty. Here, choose one simulated result to see how ARES updates its evidence and policy.

Replay telemetry is synthetic. Both paths use the same evidence engine and update the visible graph.
